classification.difficultyReason: Define two unit prices, translate two purchases into simultaneous equations, and choose an elimination or substitution procedure to obtain the drink price.

content.prompt:
Justify any conclusions and/or assumptions made in the context of the problem.

Two friends buy snacks. One buys 2 drinks and 3 chips for $\$11$, the other buys 3 drinks and 2 chips for $\$12$. How much does a drink cost?

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the price of a drink and $c$ the price of chips, in dollars. Assume both friends pay the same unit prices.
$$\begin{align*}2d+3c&=11\\3d+2c&=12\end{align*}$$
Eliminate $c$:
$$\begin{align*}4d+6c&=22\\9d+6c&=36\\5d&=14\\d&=\frac{14}{5}\\d&=2.80\end{align*}$$
A drink costs $\$2.80$.
